modify.what_it_now_forces: The sum now arrives as 4/6, so the standing instruction "Answers in simplest form" finally has an occasion to act on: the student must notice the common factor and carry out the reduction to 2/3, and a student who does not reduce leaves 4/6 on the page where it is visible rather than indistinguishable from a correct non-reducing answer. What this gives up: 1/2 + 1/3 had coprime denominators requiring an LCD found as a product, while 2 divides 6, so item 4 becomes the easier denominator subtype; that harder relationship is still exercised by item 6 (2 1/3 + 1 3/4) and item 8 (2/3 − 1/4), and item 5 and item 7 still require a true LCM of 6 and 4, so nothing that only item 4 was evidencing is lost.
